headline: Jai Corp Limited: Disclosure under SEBI Regulation 31(4) – Substantial Acquisition of Shares
sum: Jai Corp Limited has filed a mandatory disclosure under SEBI Takeover Regulations Regulation 31(4), indicating a substantial acquisition event triggering the 25% threshold notification requirement to stock exchange.
implication: A substantial shareholder (likely ≥25%) has acquired or aggregated holdings in Jai Corp, triggering mandatory open offer obligations under SEBI Takeover Code unless an exemption applies (e.g., creeping acquisition, preferential offer, or specific regulatory carve-out).
detail: Under SEBI (SAST) Regulations 2011, when an acquirer crosses 25% of a listed company's paid-up capital, a Regulation 31(4) disclosure must be filed with the exchange within two trading days. This filing initiates the takeover disclosure and open offer regime. The specific acquirer identity, stake percentage, consideration, and any exemptions claimed are contained in the filed disclosure document. Jai Corp's submission to NSE on 6 June 2026 represents compliance with this mandatory reporting requirement.

framework.ref: SEBI (Substantial Acquisition of Shares and Takeovers) Regulations, 2011, Regulation 31(4)
framework.note: Mandatory disclosure requirement when acquirer's shareholding reaches or crosses 25% of company's paid-up capital; must be filed within 2 trading days.
Definition of 'acquirer', 'group', and aggregation principles for determining when substantial acquisition threshold is crossed.
Open offer mandatory once 25% threshold is breached, except where specific exemptions apply (e.g., acquisition in open market within 30-day window, preferential offer, rights issue).
Exemptions to open offer requirement: creeping acquisition (≤5% per 12 months), permitted transactions, or regulatory carve-outs.
Conditions precedent to open offer: minimum price, publicity, escrow of shares, and minimum acceptance threshold (90% of public shareholding).
Empowers SEBI to frame takeover regulations; primary enabling statute for SEBI's regulatory authority over M&A disclosures.

framework.ref: NSE Listing Regulations (as per NSE rulebook)
framework.note: Exchange-level obligations: admission to listing, continuous disclosure of material events, and takeover-related announcements.
Form of disclosure document and acquirer disclosure; amended to include beneficial interest and pledged shareholding details.

conditions: Disclosure filed within 2 trading days of crossing 25% threshold (or as per SEBI direction)
Identity and details of acquirer/group to be disclosed
Beneficial interest and aggregation to be certified
Likely trigger: open offer obligation unless exemption claimed
approvals: Possible CCI notification if acquisition value/party structure triggers merger thresholds
Open offer compliance with SEBI & exchange oversight if triggered

triggers.note: Mandatory acquirer disclosure upon crossing 25% shareholding threshold; triggers formal takeover process under Code.
Potential open offer obligation; exemptions must be verified (creeping acquisition, preferential offer, or carve-out claimed).
If acquisition value or acquirer turnover crosses CCI thresholds (assets ≥₹1,750 cr or turnover ≥₹5,250 cr), CCI approval may be required.
If acquirer is foreign entity, RBI/FEMA approval may be required under FDI policy for sensitive sectors or entity control.
